solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be unable to find Scottish island on map at first

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another comes after it
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word map

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: Someone cannot locate a Hebridean island when first looking at the map.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose track of something so that you cannot find it is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Cryptic threat for member of the Tea Party

parts.note: the word threat jumbled gives a hatter, and mad is a common anagram signal

explanation.surface: An obscure warning aimed at a member of the US conservative Tea Party movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tea Party looks political but is the mad tea party in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's character attends the Mad Tea Party with the March Hare and the Dormouse.

clue.text: Look defeated, seeing bad house prices? Only at first

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, bad house

indicators.note: only at first asks for nothing more than the opening letter of the word prices

explanation.surface: Someone looks beaten on seeing low house prices, but only initially.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the property-market sense, a fall in house prices, but the definition is the verb for drooping in defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or droop despondently, posture collapsed, is to look beaten.

clue.text: Wartime signal that would not be misunderstood?

definitions.meaning: the siren sounded in the Second World War when an air raid was over
a message that is entirely plain, totally understood

explanation.surface: A wartime message designed to be unmistakable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the end-of-raid siren and a description of something entirely plain and lucid.

clue.text: Dependable and firm, the moment I left

parts.note: Co. is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the letter I is dropped from the word for the moment

parts.note: the instant means the present moment

explanation.surface: Describes a reliable person, steady until the very moment the speaker departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' reads as a second definition beside 'Dependable', but it is the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A constant friend is a loyal, reliable one who can always be counted on.

clue.text: Peaceful offers: "Please take up residence on British farms"

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, before it

parts.note: O is the interjection used in earnest appeals, as in O come, O hear us, a word of pleading
to live somewhere is to reside there
ranches are large farms

explanation.surface: A plea to settle on British farms as a gesture of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers of reconciliation are named after the dove's symbol of peace in the Noah story.

clue.text: Poet's program hard to break into in this way

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so the program and hard letters go within the word for in this way

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
an app is a computer program
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A poet's computer program is difficult to hack in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break into' puts APPH inside SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek lyric writer from Lesbos is a famous example of a poet.

clue.text: Pauline for one has no way to stop a detailed government plan

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the no and way letters are put inside
detailed here means de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a policy is a government plan
O is zero, nothing, no
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone named Pauline cannot find a way to block a detailed government scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means de-tailed: POLICY loses Y, and 'to stop' puts OST into A POLIC after AP. Pauline means 'of St Paul', not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's teachings and epistles are of an apostle, so Pauline is one instance of the adjective.

clue.text: Ass: it was almost quiet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: 'twere is an old contraction for it were, the subjunctive of it was
p is the musical marking piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A donkey that was nearly silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of 'TWERE, giving TWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly or foolish person is called both an ass and this informal insult.

clue.text: Chess shows one it can be a game for four

definitions.text: Chess shows one it can be a game for four

parts.words: Chess shows one it can be a game for four
parts.note: the word Chess ends in a repeated letter, SS, so it shows a pair of twin letters; the same plural also names the tennis or badminton game with two players a side

explanation.surface: Seems to say chess can be adapted for four players.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess is a two-player game, which is the misdirection: the clue is about the spelling of the word Chess, with its doubled S, and the four-player version of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis and badminton, the pairs game played by four people, two per side, has this plural name.

clue.text: Babe she gently rocked, keeping up appearances

indicators.note: rocked means shaken about, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman softly rocks an infant, while also keeping up appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes poor gentlefolk who struggle to maintain their respectability, keeping up a show of status.

clue.text: Beg one extra place to be reserved

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: something reserved is kept back inside, so the place abbreviation goes within the word for extra

parts.note: more means additional, extra
Pl. is the abbreviation for Place in street names

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for one more seat to be booked.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg and to plead are synonyms: both mean ask desperately for something.

clue.text: Shock from head of church shifting a little power to the right

indicators.note: shifting tells us one letter of the adjective for the pope is moved along
to the right says the moved letter travels later in the word, one place along

parts.note: papal means belonging to the pope, the head of the Catholic church
P is the abbreviation for power, just a little of the word

explanation.surface: A pope rocks his flock by moving a modest share of authority to the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting ... to the right' moves the first P of PAPAL one place along, giving APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock and to horrify or dismay are synonyms, both verbs.

clue.text: Egyptian leader's staff in an inn shortly needing parking

indicators.note: in places the word for staff inside the phrase an inn, shortened
shortly cuts the last letter from the word for an inn

parts.note: a hotel is an inn
staff means the workforce, the men
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A pharaoh's retinue lodges at a small inn where they need somewhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Egyptian leader' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Several pharaohs of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty bore this name, so this is a ruler of that country.

clue.text: Notice second decoration a few have received and worn

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the notice and the decoration go inside the number word

parts.note: three is a few
an ad is a notice, a short advertisement
a bar is a clasp added to a medal when it is won a second time

explanation.surface: A notice says a handful of people have been awarded a second medal and wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth worn so thin that the weave shows through is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Quality of signal in first class

definitions.meaning: how clearly a radio or TV signal is picked up
in English primary schools the first-year class of four- and five-year-olds bears this name

explanation.surface: A signal's clarity rated top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the clarity of a broadcast picked up and the British starting class at primary school.

clue.text: Centre for heretics has heart knocked out of legal defence

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter of the five-letter word for a legal defence, and it is removed

parts.note: an alibi is a defence that the accused was elsewhere

explanation.surface: A centre for heretics loses the core of its legal defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has heart knocked out of' removes the middle I of ALIBI. The Albigensians, a medieval heretic sect in southern France, were named after this town.
explanation.definitionFit: This French town was the base of the Cathar heresy crushed by the Albigensian Crusade.

clue.text: In ecstasy, composer died — really!

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A composer died in rapture, surprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or disbelief, equivalent to 'well, fancy that!', as a whole phrase.

clue.text: Complex situation in meeting as papers circulated

indicators.note: circulated suggests going round, so the paper word encircles the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A tricky situation at a meeting while documents were passed round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is the literal sense; figuratively it is an awkward, entangling predicament.

clue.text: Grain cost reduced by a penny

indicators.note: reduced by means made smaller by taking away the penny letter

parts.note: price is a cost
p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: The cost of grain comes down by a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal is a staple grain, so it is an example of the class named.

clue.text: Does he give relatively painful advice?

definitions.text: Does he give relatively painful advice?

parts.words: Does he give relatively painful advice?
parts.note: read as a family member whose advice hurts: relatively hints at a relative and painful at anguish, but it means a newspaper problem-page columnist

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man hands out advice that hurts somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean 'fairly' but points to a relative, and 'painful' points to suffering. The real person is a male agony aunt, a British term for an advice columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: A male newspaper or magazine advice columnist answering readers' personal problems is known by this phrase in Britain.

clue.text: Conflict divides work team in cave

indicators.note: divides means splitting apart, so the conflict goes into the middle of the work team

parts.note: a bee is a group gathered to work together, as in a sewing bee
war is conflict

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out among a team working in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' is not a cavern but the Latin for 'look out', old British schoolboy slang used as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave, Latin for take heed, was British schoolboy slang shouted to warn of a teacher's approach.

clue.text: Furiously thump boxing youngster, the latest of many

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the rearranged letters surround the word for a young person
furiously suggests the letters of thump are wildly thrown about

parts.note: a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: Someone angrily punches a boxing teenager, the latest in a long series of blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport the youngster does, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the umpteenth time is the latest after countless previous occasions.

clue.text: Force adopted by military group is not appropriate

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the force letter goes inside the word for a military group

parts.note: a unit is a military group
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A military group's use of force is not suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable and unsuited are synonyms of this adjective, both meaning not right for the purpose.

clue.text: Elevated construction beginning to bend in wind

indicators.note: in places the first letter of bend inside the word for wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word bend

explanation.surface: A tall structure starts to sway in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular upper wall section under a pitched roof is a raised part of a building.

clue.text: Normal sort of curve on European beauty

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the normal distribution in statistics is drawn as a bell curve

explanation.surface: A standard curve shown on a European beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Normal' looks like 'ordinary' but is the statistical normal distribution.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautiful woman, especially the most admired at a party, is a synonym of the French word.

clue.text: One liked no end to take passage in ship

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters of the word end are taken away

parts.note: a friend is one whom you like
the word end, taken as written
a gate is a passage through a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A popular person takes a sea passage aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes END away from FRIEND, leaving FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of warship, so it is an example of a vessel.

clue.text: Lost balance, carrying child — safer with this on?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the child goes inside the word for lost balance

parts.note: slid means slipped, lost one's footing
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Someone slipped while holding a child and would have been safer wearing protection.
explanation.walkthrough: SKID LID is British slang for a motorcycle crash helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash helmet makes a rider safer when worn, so the definition describes it by its purpose.

clue.text: Offer to contribute to very modest gaudy

indicators.note: contributing to here means going inside, so the word for offer is placed within the word for very modest

parts.note: tiny means very small, very modest in size
to sell is to offer goods for sale

explanation.surface: A proposal to make a small donation to something showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in cheap glittery decoration, like Christmas tinsel, is a kind of showiness.

clue.text: Regularly take in Hesiod poem

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words take in Hesiod, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Advice to read a poem by Hesiod at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Hesiod was a Greek poet, a misdirection: the epic is Virgil's Latin poem about Aeneas.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's epic about the Trojan Aeneas is a celebrated example of a poem.
